{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same invented story.","text":"Mara tightened her grip on the brass key and hurried down the narrow lane. At the far end, the old clock tower stood dark against the fading sky, its hands frozen at seven minutes past nine—the exact time her brother had vanished.

A bell rang once from somewhere inside it.

She stopped. The tower had been locked for years, ever since the town’s last clockmaker disappeared. Yet a thin blade of golden light shone beneath its door.

“Mara!” called a voice from the hill road.

She turned, but the lane behind her was empty. The voice had sounded like Tomas, though Tomas was three hundred miles away—or supposed to be. She glanced at the key. A tiny blue flame flickered in the hole at its center.

The bell rang again.

This time, every window along the lane lit up. Faces appeared behind the glass: neighbors, strangers, people she recognized from old photographs. They all watched her, perfectly still.

Mara ran to the tower and thrust the key into the lock. It turned without resistance. The door opened onto a staircase spiraling down into darkness, not up toward the clockworks.

From below came the slow scrape of footsteps.

Then Tomas spoke, close enough that she felt his breath against her cheek.

“You took your time.”

Mara leaned over the threshold. At the foot of the stairs, a familiar figure held a lantern. He looked just as he had the night he disappeared, right down to the muddy cuffs of his coat.

Behind her, the tower door began to close."}
